mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strengthening residential construction and consumer confidence, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as businesses expand and consumers spend more.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of periods when HOUST increases by at least 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and dampens corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a tight labor market that may lead to wage inflation and subsequent monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS rising and UNRATE falling fails to predict negative returns, with Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of supply chain disruption (INDPRO < 95), declining industrial production signals reduced manufacturing output and economic uncertainty, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 95.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the core inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) indicates persistent inflationary pressures that typically lead to higher interest rates and reduced equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises by at least 0.2% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 3.5%, it signals an extremely tight labor market that often precedes aggressive monetary tightening by the Fed, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE < 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in retail sales (RSAFS) and a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates strong consumer demand met with restrictive monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the market prices in the risk of a recession.
failure_condition: The joint signal of RSAFS rising and FEDFUNDS rising fails to predict negative returns, with Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing boom (HOUST > 1600), the S&P 500 tends to experience negative returns over the next 5 trading days as the market anticipates a potential correction in the real estate sector and subsequent economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of periods when HOUST > 1600.
